source_review.notes: Checked the original Popek-Goldberg paper and current Intel, AMD, Linux KVM, QEMU, Xen and RISC-V documentation for privilege, trapping, emulation, shadow translation, virtual time, binary translation and paravirtualization. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; classical results, current interface contracts, abstract models and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked guest-visible, monitor, host, abstraction, transition, exception, sensitive-set, privileged-set, exit-rate, service-demand and generation notation.
Reviewed refinement equality, classical subset condition, exit utilization and shadow-freshness relations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates the promised virtual state from implementation state and a sufficient classical condition from broader virtualization techniques.

evidence: Executed a five-instruction virtual state machine with one direct add and four intercepted operations.

Confirmed final PC 5, accumulator 6, masked control value 3, halted state, four ordered exit reasons and one device-log value; independently recomputed example exit utilization as 0.72 with port I/O contributing 0.48.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates one toy transition sequence only; it implements no ISA decoder, privilege mechanism, concurrent monitor, device isolation or timing model.

evidence: Re-derived emulation correctness as equality between the abstracted implementation transition and the promised guest transition.
Checked the sensitive-subset-of-privileged sufficient condition, reason-weighted exit utilization and equality of dependent shadow generations.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are architectural reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of a modern ISA, VMM, device model, concurrency protocol or platform.

evidence: Reviewed fault-versus-trap PC state, mutable and cross-page instruction bytes, unsupported encodings, reserved bits, aliases, concurrent vCPUs and nested faults.
Reviewed partial MMIO, pending userspace completion, interrupt edges and levels, DMA after reset, clock migration, pathological exits and side channels.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Decode, retirement, shadow, translation, device, interrupt, DMA, time, concurrency, lifecycle and assurance boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced direct and intercepted operations from virtual contract through classification, saved state, decode, validation, model transition, commit and resume.
Verified complete mediation, one retirement or specified fault, coherent shadow generations, transactional device effects, legal interrupt injection and coherent migration state.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats CPU, shadow, translation, device, interrupt, time and migration state as one virtual contract with independently owned implementation components.

evidence: Reviewed the direct and intercepted refinement cases plus explicit exception and retry subcases.
Constructed counterexamples for trap-as-emulation, boot-as-equivalence, PC-always-at-fault, shadow-as-cache, MMIO-as-memory and CPU-trapping-as-DMA-containment.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable refinement obligations, not a formal proof of an ISA, decoder, hypervisor, kernel, device, firmware or platform.

evidence: Audited uses of privileged, sensitive, sufficient, direct, intercepted, retired, faulted, equivalent, coherent and isolated.
Confirmed classical theorem claims, current architecture contracts, abstract formulas, implementation guidance, examples and assurance limits remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The classical condition is not labeled universally necessary, a trap is not labeled emulation, architectural equivalence is not labeled timing equality and complete mediation is not labeled side-channel freedom.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-081/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the state-machine toy.
Reviewed required ISA, CPU model, VMM, machine type, device, firmware, migration, differential-test, isolation and exit-distribution evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one abstract commit sequence only; it provides no evidence for processor trapping, decoder correctness, concurrency, device containment, performance or security.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed trap-and-emulate as a refinement construction combining safe direct execution with precise interception, virtual-model execution and one coherent resume state.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including exit dispatch, PC semantics, protected decode, shadow controls and translations, faults, interrupts, MMIO, DMA, clocks, multiple vCPUs, migration and differential tests. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from virtual contracts and instruction classification through the classical condition, run-intercept-emulate mechanics, shadow state, devices, time, performance, migration and assurance, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, ISA architect, hypervisor maintainer, device-model engineer, security reviewer, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
